about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Harvest is nearly done (Iowa 92%, South Dakota lagging), so harvest pressure is fading into Dec first notice; new demand is modest, with India's ethanol blending milestone a small positive for global corn use. Drought disaster designations in western Minnesota matter more for next year's soil moisture than this balance sheet.
events: Iowa soybean harvest wraps up, corn 92% done; SD lags (Brownfield)
India reaches ethanol blending milestone (World Grain)
Corn steady as first notice day approaches (Successful Farming)

soybeans.fundamental: Beans rallied with the equity rebound; harvest is complete in Iowa and some yields are record-high, so US supply is not the story. Chinese buying of US soybeans remains the main swing factor, while China's soyoil stockpiling at low domestic prices points to ample crush there.
events: Soybeans rally with equities, grains follow (AgWeb)
Record soybean yields in northeastern Illinois (Brownfield)
China stockpiles soyoil as domestic prices hit 3-month low (Bloomberg)

meal.fundamental: No meal-specific news; crush margins lean on meal as soyoil weakens with crude, which keeps meal relatively supported versus oil.
events: Soybean oil the outlier in higher soy trade (ADMIS)
What moves soybean prices: diesel and the oil share (Farm Progress)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil faces two headwinds: crude at three-month lows erodes biofuel blending economics, and China is building soyoil reserves with domestic prices at a three-month low, signalling surplus there rather than import need.
events: China stockpiles soyoil as domestic prices hit 3-month low (Bloomberg)
Soybean oil lags the soy complex (ADMIS)
Brent below $90, WTI near 3-month lows (OilPrice.com, WSJ)

wheat.fundamental: US winter wheat ratings improved for a third week, trimming crop risk for 2027, but Black Sea tensions and firmer export demand gave futures a lift overnight. Net: ample US supply vs episodic geopolitical support.
events: Winter wheat conditions improve for third straight week (USDA via AgroLatam)
Wheat futures rise on Black Sea tensions and export demand (Fastmarkets)
Wheat mixed Monday as dollar firms (Barchart, Pro Farmer)

kc.fundamental: HRW condition gains on the Plains reduce winterkill and drought worries for the 2027 crop; overnight strength comes from Black Sea headlines rather than US fundamentals.
events: Winter wheat ratings up a third week (USDA via AgroLatam)
Black Sea tensions lift wheat overnight (Fastmarkets)
KC wheat mixed against a firmer dollar (Pro Farmer)

cotton.fundamental: Texas Plains drought losses are confirmed in fresh field reports, supporting the desk's below-USDA crop view; demand news is thin and the strong dollar/weak real remain export headwinds. Focus on old-crop Mar/May.
events: Drought decimates cotton yields on the Texas Plains (Farm Progress)
Mar/May cotton spread update (Barchart)
Cotton rallies Monday morning (Barchart)

hogs.fundamental: Demand is the problem: pork values hit a six-year low and lean hogs sit near contract lows even as cash and the cutout bounced Monday. The averted port strike removes one export risk.
events: Lean hogs near contract lows on weak pork demand (The Pig Site)
Pork Board highlights ongoing demand challenges (Brownfield)
Pork and beef exports avoid disruption as port strike averted (National Hog Farmer)

cattle.fundamental: Friday's Cattle on Feed was friendly (placements -7.3%), and higher cash backs it; tight supply remains the core. Watch two-sided policy risk: rising beef imports and USDA's herd-rebuilding programme on one side, screwworm cases keeping the Mexican border closed on the other.
events: Live cattle rally on bullish COF and higher cash (AgWeb, ADMIS)
USDA approves BRAND programme for herd growth (Farms.com)
US screwworm cases surge (Reuters)

feeders.fundamental: Lower placements and the closed Mexican border keep feeder supply tight, but cheaper corn helps feedlot demand; screwworm spread is the key tail risk for both supply and sentiment.
events: Bullish COF lifts cattle complex (Barchart, ADMIS)
Screwworm cases surge, border cattle remain on hold (Reuters, RFD-TV)
USDA announces new tools for beef industry (Michigan Farm News)

class3.fundamental: Milk output still up about 2.4% y/y with cheese weak; reports of falling milk prices squeezing farm margins suggest supply growth may slow only with a lag.
events: Rising costs and falling milk prices squeeze dairy farmers (RFD-TV)
USDA cyberattack disrupts some farm payment systems (Brownfield)

class4.fundamental: No new butter/powder news; the export side gets attention from a study on EU trade barriers costing US dairy, but nothing changes near-term NDM demand.
events: Study says EU trade barriers cost US dairy billions (Feedstuffs)
Milk prices falling as costs rise (RFD-TV)

palm.fundamental: China halting palm buying as storage fills hits demand just as Malaysian stocks are well above average; crude at three-month lows also narrows the biodiesel incentive.
events: China halts palm oil purchases as storage fills (Bloomberg)
China stockpiles soyoil at 3-month-low prices (Bloomberg)
Crude near 3-month lows (WSJ)

natgas.fundamental: Milder US weather erased heating demand over the weekend; the support comes from LNG pull as Europe turns cold, though Altamira's restart slipped into December.
events: Weekend weather wipeout and HDD losses sink natgas (NGI, WSJ)
Cold Europe favours transatlantic US LNG trade (NGI)
Altamira LNG turbine repair pushed to December (NGI)

crude.fundamental: Middle East crude keeps flowing despite Gulf attacks and Hormuz mine claims, so the risk premium is draining; with OPEC+ holding December targets, the market is trading surplus talk into 2027. WTI is near three-month lows around $80.
events: Oil holds near three-month lows despite Hormuz mine claims (OilPrice.com)
Brent below $90 as banks split on 2027 outlook (OilPrice.com)
Oil falls as Middle East flows continue (WSJ)

ulsd.fundamental: Distillate stocks remain below average, keeping cracks wide even as crude falls; Red Sea/Houthi risk is the main upside driver for diesel.
events: Oil falls on supply outlook and shipping risks (WSJ)
Dangote refinery IPO plan approved (Reuters)

rbob.fundamental: US refiners ran hard and rebuilt gasoline stocks above average, compressing margins into the low-demand season; Germany's planned price cap is a small demand-side footnote.
events: America's refiners drowned their own gasoline windfall (OilPrice.com)
Germany to press ahead with gasoline price cap from 2027 (Bloomberg)
